hens_rule_text: Reno allows residents to keep chickens on their own property, but secondary sources disagree on the exact cap (numbers seen range from 6 to 12 hens); no confirmed city code limit found
permit_notes: One secondary source claims an annual hen permit is required; the city's own code enforcement contact page and a Washoe County FAQ do not confirm a permit process, only that a coop over 200 sq ft may need a building permit.
setback_notes: Secondary sources give a 20 ft setback from neighboring structures, not confirmed against the primary code text.
coop_rules: Chickens must be kept on the owner's own property with a coop for shelter; roughly 3 to 4 sq ft per bird is recommended; a coop over 200 sq ft may require a city building permit; general nuisance rules ban chickens whose noise or odor annoys the neighborhood.
zoning_notes: Reno Animal Services and Washoe County Regional Animal Services both say livestock zoning is handled separately from animal control; Reno Code Enforcement (775-334-2099) is the contact for zoning questions inside city limits, distinct from unincorporated Washoe County rules.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: The official Washoe County FAQ confirms Reno allows chickens but does not give a specific numeric cap or code section; secondary sites disagree with each other on the hen limit (6 vs 12) and on whether a permit is required, and library.municode.com style access to Reno's own municipal code text was not achieved, so the cap is left unknown rather than guessed.
